subject: Evaluation playbook & scorecard — confirmation and owners
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Hussein <samira@cordata.com>, Rajesh Menon <r.menon@novenahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Evaluation playbook & scorecard — confirmation and owners

Hi Samira / Rajesh —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a proposed evaluation playbook so we’re aligned before we produce the formal POC charter. TL;DR: hypothesis-driven scorecard, short shadow run + offline batch tests, explicit acceptance gates.

What we heard as your success criteria:
- Reduce triage latency for clinical routing by >= 40% (primary)
- Maintain clinical accuracy >= 92% on our curated set (no critical regressions)
- Keep hallucination rate < 2% on sensitive fields
- Total inference cost under $0.08 per 1k tokens (goal)

Proposed evaluation approach (high level):
1) Offline baseline: we’ll run Redwood against your redacted historical set (10k examples) to get reproducible precision/recall/false-alert numbers. Results feed into scorecard.
2) Shadow/online: 5% real traffic shadow for 2 weeks (no actions taken) to capture latency/throughput and degradation risk in live conditions.
3) Grading rubric: weighted scorecard (accuracy 40, latency 25, hallucination 20, cost 10, engineering integration effort 5). Acceptance gate = score >= 80 AND no single critical failure.
4) Rollout plan: canary -> 25% -> full; automated fallback to last-good model if error rate > 1.5% during rollout.

Timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (this week): sign-off on charter & NDA addendum
- Week 1: data handoff + baseline offline runs
- Week 2: offline scoring + review session
- Week 3-4: 2-week 5% shadow run and live metrics collection
- Week 5: acceptance review and next steps (rollout or iterate)

Ownership (recommended):
- Redwood: baseline run, model infra, scorecard templates (Ben)
- Novena: dataset provision and redaction, clinical validators (Rajesh / Samira)
- CS (Marissa): runbooks, metric dashboard, post-shadow acceptance meeting
- Success metrics & gate decisions: Karthik + Rajesh

Attachments: I’ve attached a lightweight scorecard template and an initial POC requirements worksheet for your team to complete.

Next steps I’m proposing now:
- Samira / Rajesh: confirm dataset deliverable for Week 1 (s3 link + sample schema)
- Procurement: confirm timeline for contract addendum (cc’d)
- Marissa / Karthik: confirm you can own runbooks + acceptance review on Week 5

If that looks good I’ll produce a short POC charter and send a formal calendar invitation for the kickoff.

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation playbook & scorecard — confirmation and owners

Ben —

Appreciate the clear recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we sign off on the charter: 

1) Data and privacy: our legal wants to confirm redaction scope for the offline set — we will provide a de-identified dump but need to confirm that Redwood will not retain raw PII and that SOC2 evidence will be acceptable. Can you confirm the retention policy and confirm you can sign the addendum?

2) Shadow traffic: 5% sounds reasonable. Can we cap the volume to 25k requests/day for the shadow window? We want to ensure no impact to production throttles.

3) Scoring: the weighted rubric looks good but can you add an explicit threshold for hallucination measurement (how we calculate 'hallucination rate' against free-text outputs)? We’ll share a short annotation guide for clinical validators.

We’ve attached the internal procurement checklist and a sample S3 tokenized sample for the redacted set. Procurement will take the contracting thread after we finalize the scope.

Thanks,
Samira
Head of Product — Cordata (Novena partner)
samira@cordata.com

Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation playbook & scorecard — confirmation and owners

Thanks Samira — a few operational notes and owner confirmations from Redwood: 

- Data retention: Ben, I’ll loop in Security to produce a one-page retention summary for Rajesh/Procurement and include SOC2 evidence.
- Shadow cap: we’ll throttle to 25k requests/day and instrument a circuit breaker. I’ll put the dashboard and alerts on the kickoff runbook.
- Hallucination metric: proposed approach — measure extra/incorrect entity insertions against the validator gold set; report both per-utterance and per-field hallucination rates. We’ll include an annotation schema for you to use.

Action items assigned: 
- Ben: produce POC charter doc + addendum template by EOD Thursday (2026-10-01)
- Marissa: handoff to Security for retention statement; create shadow runbook and Grafana dashboard
- Karthik: draft the acceptance-gate script and automated scoring logic (we’ll use the CSV template Ben attached as the canonical input)
- Rajesh/Samira: confirm S3 handoff and share validator team names

I’ll schedule the Week 2 offline review now for the time slots you were ok with on the call.

—Marissa

Subject: Re: Evaluation playbook & scorecard — confirmation and owners

Quick follow — I reviewed the scorecard and added two operational tweaks for clarity: 

1) Weighted targets: each metric will report both raw value and normalized score. Example: accuracy 92% -> normalized 100; latency 200ms -> normalized 90 based on agreed latency curve. This prevents gaming a single metric.
2) Acceptance gates: require score >= 80 AND no metric in the red band for two consecutive days. Also require a manual clinical sign-off for any changes that touch sensitive fields.

I’ll push a first pass of the scoring script to the drive link and wire a small notebook that converts the CSV into the dashboard-ready timeseries. Marissa — I’ll coordinate the dashboard schema with you.

Karthik
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
